note: One plain line per House 1 door, shown on the public door page. School wording, drawn from adiyogi.method_summary in each door.json. Observe-only doors get a reading line, never a practice cue. Edit here, then run npm run build:public.

lines.1: Breathe naturally and let awareness rest where the breath turns: inside after the in-breath, outside after the out-breath.
lines.2: Breathe naturally and stay present in the small space after each in-breath and each out-breath, without hurrying on.
lines.3: Rest awareness in the still centre where the breath is neither going out nor coming in. Recognise the pause; never create it.
lines.4: Observe only: read the verse and its classical description. This door is not practised.
lines.5: Rest attention at the base of the body and imagine a soft radiance rising along the centre line until it dissolves above the crown.
lines.6: Gently mark attention centre by centre up the central line, then rest in the space above the crown for a breath or two.
lines.7: Move attention up the centre line one station at a time: feel it coarsely, then subtly, then let it go and rise.
lines.8: Observe only: read the verse and its classical description. This door is not practised.
lines.9: Feel the whole field of the senses as nested rings and let the detail dissolve toward a quiet centre at the heart.
lines.10: Rest a soft gaze on empty sky or a blank wall and let attention dissolve into it, blinking whenever needed.
lines.11: Close the eyes and rest attention inside the skull as a soft field, letting steadiness build without force.
lines.12: Rest awareness on one slender channel through the middle of the body and feel its inside as open space.
lines.13: Observe only: read the verse and its classical description. This door is not practised.
lines.14: Observe only: read the verse and its classical description. This door is not practised.
lines.15: Listen past ordinary sounds to the subtle, continuous hum of a quiet room and bathe in that unbroken sound.
lines.16: Sound a soft, long Oṃ, aloud or silently, and rest in the quiet gap when the sound ends.
